messages.author: 023fa3ad935fe77a
messages.subject: Simple Code Runs in JAGS but not in Nimble
parts:
The following example runs fine with JAGS but generates errors with Nimble. Can anyone point out what I am doing wrong? Thanks.


M <- c(478,484,462,507,496,498,446,409,438,409,374,355,345,
       336,338,320,315,297,306,278,264,230,253,240,238,196,193,184,
       196,199,198,172,153,165,157,132,99
)

u <- 0.035 * M

m <- c(0.30850690, 0.30772010, 0.30680934, 0.28516078, 0.27964722, 0.27834434,
       0.26891796, 0.24924162, 0.24457801, 0.23979401, 0.23556186,
       0.21868168, 0.21468435, 0.21077073, 0.20693837, 0.19237601, 0.18891670,
       0.18552603, 0.17261481, 0.16954175, 0.16652757, 0.15229209,
       0.14960320, 0.14696430, 0.14437428, 0.13933664, 0.12980318, 0.12752724,
       0.11674930, 0.11470851, 0.11270424, 0.10503833, 0.10320631,
       0.10140678, 0.09963913, 0.07657229, 0.06314739
)


library(R2jags)

jagsdat <- data.frame(M=M,m=m,u=u)

modelA <- function() {
  for (i in 1:37) {
    M[i] ~ dnorm(mu[i],tau[i])
    mu[i] <- beta*m[i]
    tau[i] <- pow(u[i],-2)
  }
  beta ~ dlnorm(log(2000),log(3))
}

par <- c("beta")

start <- list(list("beta"=2000))
             
fit.jags <- jags(
  data=jagsdat,
  inits=start,
  parameters.to.save=par,
  n.chains=1,
  n.iter=1E+5,
  n.burnin=5000,
  model.file=modelA,
  n.thin=1
)


library(nimble)

Idata <- list(
  M = M,
  u = u,
  m = m
)

modelA <- nimbleCode( {
  for (i in 1:37) {
    M[i] ~ dnorm(mu[i],u[i])
    mu[i] <- beta*m[i]
  }
  beta ~ dlnorm(log(2000),log(3))
})

par <- c("beta")

Init <- list("beta"=2000)
             
fit.nim <- nimbleMCMC(
  modelA,
  monitors=par,
  thin = 1,
  niter = 1E+5,
  nburnin = 0,
  nchains = 1,
  check = TRUE,
  setSeed = FALSE,
  progressBar = getNimbleOption("MCMCprogressBar"),
  samples = TRUE,
  samplesAsCodaMCMC = TRUE,
  summary = TRUE,
  WAIC = FALSE
)

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: Simple Code Runs in JAGS but not in Nimble
parts:
Good question.  I appears like you didn't provide the model "constants" (right-hand-side fixed constants, in this case "m" and "u"), or the model "data" (in this case, looks like "M"), or the initial values list which you defined (Init) to the nimbleMCMC() call.  Without those values, the "model" being used in the MCMC is essentially a graphical structure with placeholders to hold all these values, but it will not find (or populate) the actual values into the model from scoping of of the variables you created in the R global environment.  Rather, you get to explicitly provide those to calls such as nimbleModel, or in your case, nimbleMCMC.

I've added those few lines below (commented with "NEW"), and it seems to run without a hitch.

Keep us posted if this works for you, and thanks for your use of NIMBLE.
library(nimble)

modelA <- nimbleCode( {
  for (i in 1:37) {
    M[i] ~ dnorm(mu[i],u[i])
    mu[i] <- beta*m[i]
  }
  beta ~ dlnorm(log(2000),log(3))
})

par <- c("beta")

Init <- list("beta"=2000)
             
fit.nim <- nimbleMCMC(
  modelA,

constants = list(m = m, u = u),    ## NEW
  data = list(M = M),                ## NEW
  inits = Init,                      ## NEW

monitors=par,
  thin = 1,
  niter = 1E+5,
  nburnin = 0,
  nchains = 1,
  check = TRUE,
  setSeed = FALSE,
  progressBar = getNimbleOption("MCMCprogressBar"),
  samples = TRUE,
  samplesAsCodaMCMC = TRUE,
  summary = TRUE,
  WAIC = FALSE
)

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Simple Code Runs in JAGS but not in Nimble
parts:
It looks like you want Q*u[i] to be the standard deviation.  In JAGS, you create tau = precision = 1/(Q*u[i])^2.  In nimble it looks like you are using Q*u[i] and expecting it to be standard deviation.

nimble uses the same default parameterization as BUGS/JAGS, not R.  It does extend BUGS/JAGS by supporting alternative parameterizations via named parameters. Therefore the models you've used are not the same.  In nimble you are saying precision = Q*u[i].  It looks like what you intend is 

M[i] ~ dnorm(mu[i], sd = Q*u[i])

Distributions and parameterizations are described in the nimble User Manual available at r-nimble.org.

-Perry

    M[i] ~ dnorm(mu[i],tau[i])
    mu[i] <- beta*m[i]
    tau[i] <- pow(u[i],-2)
  }
  beta ~ dlnorm(log(2000),log(3))
}

par <- c("beta")

start <- list(list("beta"=2000))
             
fit.jags <- jags(
  data=jagsdat,
  inits=start,
  parameters.to.save=par,
  n.chains=1,
  n.iter=1E+5,
  n.burnin=5000,
  model.file=modelA,
  n.thin=1
)


library(nimble)

Idata <- list(
  M = M,
  u = u,
  m = m
)

modelA <- nimbleCode( {
  for (i in 1:37) {
    M[i] ~ dnorm(mu[i],u[i])
    mu[i] <- beta*m[i]
  }
  beta ~ dlnorm(log(2000),log(3))
})

par <- c("beta")

Init <- list("beta"=2000)
             
fit.nim <- nimbleMCMC(
  modelA,
  monitors=par,
  thin = 1,
  niter = 1E+5,
  nburnin = 0,
  nchains = 1,
  check = TRUE,
  setSeed = FALSE,
  progressBar = getNimbleOption("MCMCprogressBar"),
  samples = TRUE,
  samplesAsCodaMCMC = TRUE,
  summary = TRUE,
  WAIC = FALSE
)
